result.markdown:
# Nationwide Slow Data and Traffic Dip Due to Core DNS Software Upgrade

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** bad_change at `CORE-DNS-01`
- **Confidence:** medium (Directly evidenced by change log, KPIs, and alarms on CORE-DNS-01 matching the timing of the anomaly.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-18 15:00 to 2026-09-18 16:30
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-18 13:59
- **Affected:** CORE-DNS-01, S-SAH-001, S-SAH-002, S-SAH-003, S-SAH-004

## Summary

Software upgrade CHG-2026-0043 on CORE-DNS-01 caused DNS degradation, leading to nationwide slow data and traffic drops.

Nationwide slow data and traffic dip affecting 48 sites and core DNS resolution.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-18 13:59: Software upgrade applied to CORE-DNS-01. [CHG-2026-0043]
- 2026-09-18 15:00: Nationwide traffic and DNS query success drop anomaly starts. [ALR-0021, T5]
- 2026-09-18 15:08: Major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE alarm raised on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000365]
- 2026-09-18 16:30: Impact recovery and anomaly ends. [ALR-0021, T5]

## Evidence

- All regions share a single DNS node CORE-DNS-01 affecting all data sessions when slowed. [RB-DNS-DEGRADATION#01]
- CORE-DNS-01 query_success_pct dropped to 85.7 at worst. [ANM-000238]
- CORE-DNS-01 resolution_ms spiked to 175 ms. [T5]
- No maintenance window was scheduled on any node during the incident. [T3]

## Hypotheses

1. **bad_change** at CORE-DNS-01: confirmed. Software upgrade CHG-2026-0043 preceded the DNS degradation and KPI drop on CORE-DNS-01. [CHG-2026-0043, T5]
2. **core_degradation** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. The degradation was directly triggered by the software change rather than spontaneous core failure. [CHG-2026-0043]

## Ruled out

- CHG-2026-0044: Upgrade on CORE-AMF-01 did not directly cause DNS resolution failures.
- CHG-2026-0045: Upgrade on CORE-UPF-01 was unrelated to the DNS resolution timeout symptoms.

## Recommended actions

- Monitor CORE-DNS-01 resolver service stability following patch applications.
- Review software upgrade rollback procedures for core DNS services.

## Sources

- `ALM-000365`: major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE on CORE-DNS-01, raised 2026-09-18 15:08, cleared 2026-09-18 16:38
- `RB-DNS-DEGRADATION#01`: Core DNS degradation > Overview: All regions share a single DNS node (`node_type` `core_dns`, id `CORE-DNS-01`). When it slows down or drops queries, every d...
- `ANM-000238`: CORE-DNS-01 query_success_pct drop, z -125.4, baseline 99.9 -> 85.7
- `T3`: get_maintenance(start=2026-09-18 12:00, end=2026-09-18 18:00, include_ancestors=True) -> No maintenance window scheduled on any node between 2026-09-18 12:00 and 2026-09-18 18:00.
- `CHG-2026-0044`: software_upgrade on CORE-AMF-01 at 2026-09-18 14:01: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-AMF-01 (service restart)
- `CHG-2026-0045`: software_upgrade on CORE-UPF-01 at 2026-09-18 14:02: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-UPF-01 (service restart)

report.title: Nationwide Slow Data and Traffic Dip Due to Core DNS Software Upgrade

confounders.why: Harmless software_upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 completed 54 min before the degradation; the DNS KPIs stayed normal until the onset and the same patch on other core nodes did nothing.

truth.notes: trap=change_on_root_node; CORE-DNS-01 degraded for about 99 min; nationwide latency up, volume down, RRC unaffected. Trap: a software upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 itself ran 54 min before the onset, so a hasty investigator blames the change. Settled by: (1) the DNS and RRC KPIs were normal for 54 min after the upgrade, while a configuration change takes effect at once; (2) the same patch under the same ticket went onto CORE-AMF-01 and CORE-UPF-01 at the same time and both stayed healthy; (3) the degradation ended by itself, with no rollback or other change at the recovery.
